title: Modules over $\kunZn$ have invertible orders
statement:
Let $K$ be a field and $n\in I_K$ an integer invertible in $K$
([def-kun-torsion-invertible]), and put $\Lambda=\mathbf Z/n\mathbf Z$
(the coefficient ring denoted $\kunZn$). For every scheme $T$ over $K$,
every sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on the small etale site of $T$
[def-weil-pbc-etale-site], in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves],
has orders invertible in $K$ as defined in [def-kun-torsion-invertible].

proof.text:
Let $F$ be the given sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules. Write $\mathcal O=\Lambda_T$ for the constant sheaf of rings. By [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves] and [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], each $F(U)$ is an $\mathcal O(U)$-module. The canonical constant-section ring homomorphism $\Lambda\to\mathcal O(U)$ given by the sheafification morphism of [def-weil-pbc-sheafification] applied to the constant presheaf in [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf] sends $1$ to $1$. Since $n\cdot1_\Lambda=0$, it follows that $n\cdot1_{\mathcal O(U)}=0$. The module axioms now give, for every section $s\in F(U)$,
$$n s=(n\cdot1_{\mathcal O(U)})s=0s=0.$$
Here the first equality is obtained by adding $1s=s$ to itself $n$ times; no assertion about exactness or preservation of colimits is used.

source.place: ## Proof, first two sentences: the coefficient ring and every section are killed by n; elementary expansion

proof.text:
Fix a geometric point $\bar t$ of $T$ and use the abelian-group colimit defining $F_{\bar t}$ in [def-weil-pbc-geometric-stalks]. Its cocone maps $\iota_U:F(U)\to F_{\bar t}$ are additive. For an additive map $f:A\to B$, induction on $n$ gives $f(na)=nf(a)$: the case $0$ is $f(0)=0$, and the successor case follows from $f(na+a)=f(na)+f(a)$. Thus multiplication by $n$ is an abelian-group endomorphism of the stalk and, for every section $s\in F(U)$, step 1 gives
$$[n]_{F_{\bar t}}(\iota_U(s))=\iota_U(ns)=\iota_U(0)=0.$$
The endomorphisms $[n]_{F_{\bar t}}$ and $0$ therefore have identical composites with every map of the defining cocone. The uniqueness clause of that colimit's universal property gives $[n]_{F_{\bar t}}=0$, so every stalk element is killed by $n$.

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence: every geometric-stalk element is killed by n; elementary colimit calculation

proof.text: By [def-kun-torsion-invertible], $n\in I_K$ includes $n\geq1$ and $n\cdot1_K\ne0$. The sectionwise annihilation in step 1 makes the underlying abelian sheaf torsion in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-etale-sheaves]: for each section take the identity covering and the positive annihilator $n$. For every geometric point and every stalk element, step 2 supplies the annihilator $n\in I_K$. This is precisely the definition in [def-kun-torsion-invertible] of having orders invertible in $K$.

source.place: ## Proof, last sentence: apply the definition of orders invertible in K

lean.statement: theorem zmodSheaf_hasFieldInvertibleOrders (K : Type u) [Field K] (n : Etale.invertibleTorsionOrders K) (T : Over (Spec (.of K))) (F : SheafOfModules.{u + 1} ((constantSheaf T.left.smallEtaleTopology RingCat.{u + 1}).obj (RingCat.of (ULift.{u + 1} (ZMod n.val))))) : Etale.IsTorsionOfInvertibleOrder K T ((SheafOfModules.toSheaf _).obj F)
lean.note: Uses the published def-kun-torsion-invertible interface in Sheaf.AlgebraicGeometry.InvertibleTorsionOrders: Etale.invertibleTorsionOrders and Etale.IsTorsionOfInvertibleOrder. Bundled Over encodes an arbitrary K-scheme; the constant-ring-sheaf module encoding is unchanged.
